newsitem.title: USA: Dayton divisions contribute to Q1 net rise.
newsitem.headline: Dayton divisions contribute to Q1 net rise.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said Tuesday that higher earnings for the first quarter ended May 3 were due to improved results in each of the retailer's divisions.
Earlier, it reported earnings of $0.53 per fully diluted share before a $0.09 a share charge, up from $0.16 a year ago.

"We are pleased with our results in the first quarter, especially Target's strong performance," Bob Ulrich, Dayton Hudson chairman, said in a statement. "Each of our divisions contributed to our improvement in earnings this quarter."

First quarter operating profit for the company increased 68 percent to $337 million compared with $200 million in first quarter 1996. Total revenues increased nine percent to $5.89 billion, compared with $5.38 billion last year. Comparable-store revenues increased four percent.

Dayton said its Target division's operating profit in the quarter increased 88 percent to $251 million, compared with $133 million in the same period in 1996. Target's total revenues increased 14 percent and comparable-store revenues were up six percent.

The company said its Mervyn's division's operating profit increased 30 percent in first quarter 1997 to $51 million, compared with $39 million in first quarter 1996. Revenues decreased two percent and comparable-store revenues were even compared with last year.

First quarter operating profit at the Department Store Division increased 26 percent to $35 million, compared with $28 million in 1996. Total revenues were even compared with last year and comparable-store revenues declined three percent.

Dayton said it first quarter after-tax charge of $21 million or $0.09 a share resulted from the repurchase of approximately $250 million of long-term debt. This debt has been replaced with lower interest rate debt.
As a result, the company expects interest savings of $7 million, or $0.02 a share, on an annual basis.
